ing: or sour cream mixed with cream cheese
st: Mix the ground beef, lamb, grated onion, garlic, baking soda, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the sparkling water and knead with wet hands for 5 minutes until the mixture is sticky and smooth.
Cover and chill for at least [[1 hour]] to let the flavors blend.
Wet your hands and roll the meat into 16 small sausages, about 3 inches long and as thick as your thumb.
Heat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat and oil it lightly.
Grill the ćevapi for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Warm the flatbread on the grill for 30 seconds on each side.
Serve 4 ćevapi in each flatbread with the kajmak and chopped onion.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, salt, and pepper. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until cooked through to 160°F (71°C) and dry. Cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Oil a large round baking pan or 9 by 13 inch pan.
Mix the remaining oil with the warm water in a bowl for brushing.
Lay a phyllo sheet on the counter. Brush with the oil mix and spoon a line of meat along one long edge.
Roll up the sheet into a long thin rope, brushing as you go. Coil it into a spiral in the pan.
Repeat with the remaining sheets, joining the spiral coils so they touch. Brush the top with the remaining oil mix.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp.
Cool for 10 minutes, cut into wedges, and serve warm.
Put the chicken, carrot, celery, onion, [[2 tsp]] salt, and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 35 minutes.
Lift the chicken out and shred the meat once it is cool enough to handle. Discard the bones and skin.
Add the sliced okra to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes until tender.
Melt the butter in a small pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Whisk [[2 cups]] of hot broth into the roux until smooth, then stir it back into the soup. Simmer 5 minutes to thicken.
In a bowl, mix the egg yolks, sour cream, and lemon juice. Slowly whisk in a ladle of hot soup to warm it up.
Take the soup off the heat. Stir in the egg mixture and the shredded chicken. Do not boil after this or it will curdle.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Choose a large heavy pot or Dutch oven with a tight lid.
Put the beef and lamb in the bottom of the pot. Add the onions, garlic, salt, and peppercorns.
Layer the carrots, then the cabbage wedges, potatoes, bell pepper, and tomatoes on top of the meat.
Pour in the water, sprinkle on the parsley, and cover tightly.
Bake for 3 hours without stirring, until the meat is falling apart tender.
Check once after 2 hours. Add a splash of hot water if it looks dry.
Rest 10 minutes. Serve straight from the pot with bread.
Rinse the grape leaves and drain them. Trim off any thick stems.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onions for 6 minutes until soft. Cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the onions with the beef, rice, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Place a leaf shiny side down and put 1 tablespoon of filling near the stem end. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Line a wide pot with a few spare leaves and pack the rolls in tightly, seam side down.
Pour over the hot water and lemon juice and weigh the rolls down with a plate.
Cover and simmer gently for 50 minutes. The beef should reach 160°F (71°C) and the rice should be soft.
Rest 10 minutes before serving warm with yogurt.

ing: divided, plus more for the water
st: Mix the flour, egg, water, and [[1 tsp]] salt into a stiff dough. Knead 8 minutes, then wrap and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the beef, grated onion, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and pepper for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 2-inch squares.
Put a pinch of filling in the middle of each square and pinch the corners together to make small sealed pockets.
Stir the garlic into the yogurt with a pinch of salt and let it sit at room temperature.
Boil the dumplings in a large pot of salted water for 10 minutes, until they float and the beef is cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Melt the butter in a small pan and stir in the paprika.
Drain the dumplings, top with the garlic yogurt, then drizzle with the paprika butter.
Peel the onions and cut a slit from top to bottom, down to the center. Boil them in salted water for 10 minutes until soft.
Drain and cool, then peel the layers apart one by one. Keep the 3 or 4 outer sheets from each onion, and chop any leftover inner layers.
Mix the beef, rice, garlic, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, paprika, salt, pepper, parsley, and the chopped onion.
Place a spoonful of filling on each onion layer and roll up snugly.
Pack the rolls seam side down in a wide pot, in one tight layer.
Mix the hot water, oil, and remaining [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, and pour over the rolls.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 50 minutes, until the beef is cooked through to 160°F (71°C) and the rice is tender.
Serve warm with some of the cooking juices.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and oil and stir to make a soft dough. Knead 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise for [[1 hour]] in a warm spot until doubled.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and let them rest 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) with a baking sheet inside.
Flatten each ball into a disc about 5 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick. Use your fingers to press a pattern of lines or a dimple in the top.
Brush with the water and sprinkle with the nigella seeds. Let them rise for [[20 minutes]].
Slide them onto the hot sheet and bake for 12 minutes until puffed and golden. Eat warm.
Peel the apples and cut out the core from the top with a small spoon, leaving the bottom closed. Rub with lemon juice to stop browning.
In a pot just big enough for the apples, simmer [[0.75 cup]] of the sugar with the water and lemon peel for 5 minutes.
Add the apples, cover, and poach gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until tender but still holding their shape.
Lift the apples out carefully and cool. Keep the syrup.
Mix the ground walnuts with [[0.25 cup]] sugar and 2 tablespoons of the syrup to make a thick paste.
Stuff the paste into the apple cavities.
Simmer the remaining syrup for 10 minutes until it thickens, then spoon over the apples. Chill for [[1 hour]].
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla to soft peaks and put a dollop on each apple before serving.
Cream the butter and powdered sugar for 3 minutes. Beat in the egg and lemon zest.
Mix the flour and baking powder, then work into the butter mixture to make a soft dough. Chill for [[30 minutes]].
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Pinch off walnut-sized pieces and roll each into a 2-inch oval, like a date.
Press each with the back of a fork or a knife tip to mark lines on the top.
Bake on a lined sheet for 20 minutes until golden. Cool for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the sugar, water, and lemon juice for 10 minutes until slightly syrupy. Let it cool until warm.
Put the warm cookies into the syrup and soak for 5 minutes, turning once.
Lift out and arrange on a platter. Sprinkle with the chopped walnuts and let them set before serving.
Heat the broiler or oven to 475°F (245°C). Lay the whole peppers and the eggplant (pricked with a fork) on foil-lined trays.
Roast, turning every 10 minutes, for 40 minutes, until the peppers are blistered and black in spots and the eggplant has collapsed.
Put the roasted peppers in a covered bowl and steam for [[15 minutes]]. This loosens the skins.
Peel the peppers, remove the seeds and stems, and scoop the eggplant flesh from its skin. Drain in a colander for 10 minutes.
Chop the vegetables well or pulse them in a food processor to a coarse puree.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the puree and garlic and cook, stirring, for 30 minutes until thick and dark.
Stir in the vinegar, salt, and pepper and cook 5 more minutes.
Cool, then store in a clean jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Serve with bread or grilled meat.
